The main takeaway from our work is that
the motherhood penalty is a phenomenon of the labour market rather than of the family.
, although the motherhood penalty exists in most countries, the extent to which it affects low-educated mothers varies greatly between countries.
the motherhood penalty in employment is a complex phenomenon, and it is not always the case that mothers are less likely to be employed than women without children.
